_comment: Quran.ws Terminology Standard, snapshot 499bc74667765196. Every entry below is a decision, with its reason. The renames themselves are in the git history; this file records only what the audit is told to read past, and why.
_exclude: tools/texts/qc is the DigitalKhatt text exactly as published (symlinks into .cache/words) — the publisher's transliterations, not names this project chose. atlas.json carries the surahs' English names, which are glosses a reader sees, not identifiers. tools/data/qiraat-ayah-map is a checked-out copy of quranpedia/qiraat-ayah-map: its file, key and member names belong to that project. tools/terminology is a pinned copy of the standard itself, vendored so CI can run the gate without credentials for the private guidelines repo; it lists every spelling of every concept by design, so auditing it is noise. docs/defects, docs/demo and scratchpad were removed from the repository and its history: they were generated output and mid-work material, and the generators that wrote them ARE audited.
_ignore_words: Each of these means something else here, verified site by site: `pos` is a word's ordinal inside its ayah — the third number of a word_key — and never a part of speech; `part`/`parts` are path segments and string pieces, never a juz (the juz is named `juz` throughout); `mad` is the Median Absolute Deviation of tools/refdb.py's page registration, not the madd; `reading` is reading ORDER (right-to-left) and `readings` its plural, never a qiraah — the qiraah is named `qiraah`; `simple` is http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler and 'a simple pass'; `stop`/`stops` are the English verb ('a span that stops short'); `lin` is a local in audit_inkidentity.py, not madd al-lin; `diacritics` is used for ALL marks together (harakat, dots and dabt), which is broader than harakah; `orthography` is the ordinary English word in a sentence about open tanwin; `elephant` is the surah's English gloss in a reader-facing list; `chapter`/`chapters` name quran.com's /api/v4/chapters endpoint and the cache built from it; `timing` is a generic build timing. Where any of these DID mean the Quranic concept, it was renamed rather than ignored. `g_ayah` is the audit reading the CSS selector `g.ayah-fragment` — the group WAS `g.ayah` and is now correct, but the recorded alias still matches its prefix; `rub` is prose writing the quarter as rubʿ, while every identifier is `rubu_al_hizb`. `waqf_jaiz` is the same shape as `g_ayah`: the deprecated name is a prefix of the canonical `waqf_jaiz_mustawi_al_tarafayn` this tree now writes, so the audit matches the corrected name. `merging` is merging ligature CUTS and merging two audits' rows, never idgham (the tajwid ruling is named `idgham`); `nasalisation` and `lengthening` are the English column of docs/reference/mushaf-signs, which exists to say in English what ghunnah and madd are. `word_by_word` is the third of the `g_ayah`/`waqf_jaiz` shape: the deprecated name is a strict prefix of the canonical `word_by_word_translation`, so the audit matches the very phrase the standard asks for — the demo's prose writes “word-by-word translation” in running English, which IS the concept's name spelled out for a reader. Every identifier is `word_by_word_translation`. This is also the rule that garbled the prose once: a blind wbw → word_by_word_translation substitution turned “word-by-word translation sets” into “word-by-word-translation-translation sets” on the published demo.
_allow_gloss_in: The reader library is the UI layer: a button that says Pause the recitation, and prose explaining what an ayah is, are display, not identifiers. The audio element's own pause() is the DOM's name and not ours at all. Wrong spellings and deprecated names are still errors here.
_external_names: Locators. quran.com's word and verse fields are read verbatim out of .cache/words/page-*.json and out of its API; `verse-N` is the id the upstream artwork gives its own ayah polygons, and tools/build_ayah_polygons.py matches on it; the rest are package, font and repository names. Changing a letter of any of them breaks the reference. What this project calls the same thing once it has read it IS renamed: the word record's own fields are rasm_uthmani and rasm_imlai, and its key is a word_key. The mushaf edition slugs (qalon-kfqc, douri-kfqc) and the screenshot filenames name directories in quranpedia/quran-svg's own mushafs/ tree, which this repo reads but does not own. Word-By-Word-Quran-Android, qari-stats and AL-Khatma are other projects' own names, listed in the shipping survey. `verse-` is the prefix of the artwork's polygon ids, matched by a regex literal in tools/build_ayah_polygons.py and tools/audit_ayah_polygons.py; /verses/by_page is quran.com's endpoint. The UthmanicHafs release writes its own `suras`, `ayat` and `sura` keys (docs/HAFS-JSON-SOURCE.md); tools/build_word_by_word_translation_seg.py reads them as the publisher spells them. `ayah_markers` is the id quranpedia/quran-svg gives the group holding the medallions; the pipeline finds the group by that id and emits g.ayah-mark from it. `verses_count` and `bismillah_pre` are quran.com's own chapter fields, read in tools/quran_meta.py. `aya_text`, `aya_no` and `sura_no` are the UthmanicHafs release's own column names in .cache/official/hafsData_v2-0.json, read as the publisher writes them. `data-aya` is MushafDatabase V1.01's own attribute name for the ayah number (V1.0 wrote `data-ayah`); tools/refdb.py and tools/audit_reference.py read both as the publisher writes them.
